body.en: While differentiation is governed by deterministic rules (product, quotient, chain), integration is fundamentally an inverse operation requiring tactical pattern recognition. Standard antiderivative tables cover elementary functions; for composite, product, rational, and radical expressions, analytical techniques must be systematically deployed to transform non-trivial integrands into solvable algebraic forms.
body.ar: While differentiation is governed by deterministic rules (product, quotient, chain), integration is fundamentally an inverse operation requiring tactical pattern recognition. Standard antiderivative tables cover elementary الدوال; for composite, product, rational, and radical expressions, analytical techniques must be systematically deployed to transform non-trivial integrands into solvable algebraic forms.

label.en: ▲ Theorem 6.1 — Integration by Substitution (Reverse Chain Rule)
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 6.1 — Integration by Substitution (Reverse Chain Rule)

body.en:
Let \(g:[a,b] \to I\) be continuously differentiable on \([a,b]\), and let \(f:I \to \mathbb{R}\) be continuous on an interval \(I\). If \(u = g(x)\), then \(du = g'(x)\,dx\), and the indefinite integral satisfies:

\[ \int f\big(g(x)\big)\,g'(x)\,dx = \int f(u)\,du = F(u) + C = F\big(g(x)\big) + C \]

For definite integrals, transforming the variable simultaneously transforms the boundary limits:

\[ \int_a^b f\big(g(x)\big)\,g'(x)\,dx = \int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)\,du \]

Analytical Proof

Let \(F\) be an antiderivative of \(f\), so that \(F'(u) = f(u)\). Define the composite function \(H(x) = F(g(x))\). By the Chain Rule of differential calculus:

\[ H'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\big[F(g(x))\big] = F'(g(x))\cdot g'(x) = f(g(x))\,g'(x) \]

By the First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, integrating \(H'(x)\) with respect to \(x\) recovers \(H(x)\):

\[ \int f(g(x))\,g'(x)\,dx = H(x) + C = F(g(x)) + C = \int f(u)\,du \]

Applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to definite evaluation on \([a,b]\):

\[ \int_a^b f(g(x))g'(x)\,dx = \big[F(g(x))\big]_a^b = F(g(b)) - F(g(a)) = \int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)\,du \quad \blacksquare \]
body.ar:
Let \(g:[a,b] \to I\) be continuously differentiable on \([a,b]\), and let \(f:I \to \mathbb{R}\) be continuous on an interval \(I\). If \(u = g(x)\), then \(du = g'(x)\,dx\), and the indefinite التكامل satisfies:

\[ \int f\big(g(x)\big)\,g'(x)\,dx = \int f(u)\,du = F(u) + C = F\big(g(x)\big) + C \]

For definite التكاملات, transforming the المتغير simultaneously transforms the boundary النهايات:

\[ \int_a^b f\big(g(x)\big)\,g'(x)\,dx = \int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)\,du \]

Analytical Proof

Let \(F\) be an antiderivative of \(f\), so that \(F'(u) = f(u)\). Define the composite الدالة \(H(x) = F(g(x))\). By the Chain Rule of differential التفاضل والتكامل:

\[ H'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\big[F(g(x))\big] = F'(g(x))\cdot g'(x) = f(g(x))\,g'(x) \]

By the First Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل, integrating \(H'(x)\) بالنسبة إلى \(x\) recovers \(H(x)\):

\[ \int f(g(x))\,g'(x)\,dx = H(x) + C = F(g(x)) + C = \int f(u)\,du \]

Applying the Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل to definite evaluation on \([a,b]\):

\[ \int_a^b f(g(x))g'(x)\,dx = \big[F(g(x))\big]_a^b = F(g(b)) - F(g(a)) = \int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)\,du \quad \blacksquare \]

label.en: ▲ Theorem 6.2 — Integration by Parts (Reverse Product Rule)
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 6.2 — Integration by Parts (Reverse Product Rule)

body.en:
Let \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\) be continuously differentiable functions on an interval \([a,b]\). The indefinite integral satisfies:

\[ \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du \]

and the definite integral satisfies:

\[ \int_a^b u(x)\,v'(x)\,dx = \big[u(x)v(x)\big]_a^b - \int_a^b v(x)\,u'(x)\,dx \]

Analytical Proof

Recall the Product Rule for differentiation. For functions \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\):

\[ \frac{d}{dx}\big[u(x)v(x)\big] = u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x) \]

Integrating both sides with respect to \(x\):

\[ \int \frac{d}{dx}\big[u(x)v(x)\big]\,dx = \int u'(x)v(x)\,dx + \int u(x)v'(x)\,dx \]

By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, the left-hand side is \(u(x)v(x)\). Using differential notation \(du = u'(x)\,dx\) and \(dv = v'(x)\,dx\):

\[ u(x)v(x) = \int v\,du + \int u\,dv \]

Subtracting \(\int v\,du\) from both sides produces the classical integration by parts formula:

\[ \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du \quad \blacksquare \]
body.ar:
Let \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\) be continuously differentiable الدوال on an interval \([a,b]\). The indefinite التكامل satisfies:

\[ \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du \]

and the definite التكامل satisfies:

\[ \int_a^b u(x)\,v'(x)\,dx = \big[u(x)v(x)\big]_a^b - \int_a^b v(x)\,u'(x)\,dx \]

Analytical Proof

Recall the Product Rule for differentiation. For الدوال \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\):

\[ \frac{d}{dx}\big[u(x)v(x)\big] = u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x) \]

Integrating both sides بالنسبة إلى \(x\):

\[ \int \frac{d}{dx}\big[u(x)v(x)\big]\,dx = \int u'(x)v(x)\,dx + \int u(x)v'(x)\,dx \]

By the Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل, the left-hand side is \(u(x)v(x)\). Using differential notation \(du = u'(x)\,dx\) and \(dv = v'(x)\,dx\):

\[ u(x)v(x) = \int v\,du + \int u\,dv \]

Subtracting \(\int v\,du\) from both sides produces the classical integration by parts الصيغة:

\[ \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du \quad \blacksquare \]

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Techniques of Integration)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Techniques of Integration)

body.en:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts formula:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product derivative: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).
body.ar:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts الصيغة:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product المشتقة: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).

label.en: Worked Example 6.1 — Foundations: Definite Substitution & Limit Transformation
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.1 — Foundations: Definite Substitution & النهاية Transformation

body.en:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^1 x^2 \sqrt{x^3 + 1}\,dx\).

Step 1: Identify inner composite function and differential.
Let \(u = x^3 + 1\). Then \(du = 3x^2\,dx\), which implies \(x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{3}\,du\).

Step 2: Transform limits of integration.
When \(x = 0\), \(u = 0^3 + 1 = 1\).
When \(x = 1\), \(u = 1^3 + 1 = 2\).

Step 3: Integrate in terms of \(u\).

\[ \int_0^1 x^2 \sqrt{x^3 + 1}\,dx = \frac{1}{3} \int_1^2 u^{1/2}\,du = \frac{1}{3} \left[ \frac{2}{3}u^{3/2} \right]_1^2 = \frac{2}{9}\big(2^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}\big) = \frac{2(2\sqrt{2} - 1)}{9} \]
body.ar:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^1 x^2 \sqrt{x^3 + 1}\,dx\).

Step 1: Identify inner composite الدالة and differential.
Let \(u = x^3 + 1\). Then \(du = 3x^2\,dx\), which implies \(x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{3}\,du\).

Step 2: Transform النهايات of integration.
When \(x = 0\), \(u = 0^3 + 1 = 1\).
When \(x = 1\), \(u = 1^3 + 1 = 2\).

Step 3: Integrate in terms of \(u\).

\[ \int_0^1 x^2 \sqrt{x^3 + 1}\,dx = \frac{1}{3} \int_1^2 u^{1/2}\,du = \frac{1}{3} \left[ \frac{2}{3}u^{3/2} \right]_1^2 = \frac{2}{9}\big(2^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}\big) = \frac{2(2\sqrt{2} - 1)}{9} \]

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations
Evaluate the indefinite integral \(\displaystyle \int \frac{\cos(\ln x)}{x}\,dx\) for \(x > 0\).
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations
احسب قيمة the indefinite integral \(\displaystyle \int \frac{\cos(\ln x)}{x}\,dx\) for \(x > 0\).

solution.en:
Substitute \(u = \ln x\). The derivative is \(du = \frac{1}{x}\,dx\).
The integral simplifies directly to:
\[ \int \cos(u)\,du = \sin(u) + C = \sin(\ln x) + C \]

label.en: ▲ Protocol 6.3 — The LIATE Heuristic & Tabular Integration
label.ar: ▲ Protocol 6.3 — The LIATE Heuristic & Tabular Integration (طرق وتقنيات التكامل المتقدمة)

body.en:
When executing integration by parts \(\int u\,dv\), prioritize the choice of \(u\) using the LIATE hierarchy:

  1. L: Logarithmic functions (\(\ln x, \log_b x\))
  2. I: Inverse trigonometric functions (\(\arcsin x, \arctan x\))
  3. A: Algebraic / polynomial functions (\(x^n, 3x^2 + 1\))
  4. T: Trigonometric functions (\(\sin x, \cos x\))
  5. E: Exponential functions (\(e^x, 2^x\))

Functions appearing earlier in the list differentiate into simpler algebraic forms, making them optimal choices for \(u\). Functions later in the list integrate easily without increasing complexity, making them ideal for \(dv\).

Tabular Method (Polynomial \(\times\) Trig / Exponential): When \(u = P(x)\) is an \(n\)-th degree polynomial, successive differentiation terminates at 0 after \(n+1\) steps. Alternate signs \((+, -, +, -)\) across diagonal products \(u^{(k)} \int^{(k+1)} v\) to compute multi-step antiderivatives in a single compact matrix.
body.ar:
When executing integration by parts \(\int u\,dv\), prioritize the choice of \(u\) using the LIATE hierarchy:

  1. L: Logarithmic الدوال (\(\ln x, \log_b x\))
  2. I: Inverse trigonometric الدوال (\(\arcsin x, \arctan x\))
  3. A: Algebraic / كثيرة الحدود الدوال (\(x^n, 3x^2 + 1\))
  4. T: Trigonometric الدوال (\(\sin x, \cos x\))
  5. E: Exponential الدوال (\(e^x, 2^x\))

Functions appearing earlier in the list differentiate into simpler algebraic forms, making them optimal choices for \(u\). الدوال later in the list integrate easily without increasing complexity, making them ideal for \(dv\).

Tabular Method (كثيرة الحدود \(\times\) Trig / Exponential): عندما \(u = P(x)\) is an \(n\)-th degree كثيرة الحدود, successive differentiation terminates at 0 after \(n+1\) steps. Alternate signs \((+, -, +, -)\) across diagonal products \(u^{(k)} \int^{(k+1)} v\) to compute multi-step antiderivatives in a single compact المصفوفة.

label.en: ▲ Theorem 6.4 — Partial Fraction Decomposition & Trigonometric Substitutions
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 6.4 — Partial Fraction Decomposition & Trigonometric Substitutions

body.en:
Rational Functions (Partial Fractions): Let \(P(x)/Q(x)\) be a proper rational function with \(\deg(P) < \deg(Q)\). By the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, \(Q(x)\) factors over \(\mathbb{R}\) into products of linear factors \((ax+b)^m\) and irreducible quadratic factors \((ax^2+bx+c)^n\):

  • Distinct linear factor \((x-r)\): produces term \(\frac{A}{x-r}\).
  • Repeated linear factor \((x-r)^k\): produces \(\frac{A_1}{x-r} + \frac{A_2}{(x-r)^2} + \dots + \frac{A_k}{(x-r)^k}\).
  • Irreducible quadratic factor \(x^2+px+q\): produces term \(\frac{Ax+B}{x^2+px+q}\).

If \(\deg(P) \ge \deg(Q)\), polynomial long division must be executed first to express \(P/Q = S(x) + R(x)/Q(x)\) with \(\deg(R) < \deg(Q)\).

Trigonometric Substitutions (Radical Elimination):

  • \(\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} \implies x = a\sin\theta,\quad dx = a\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{a^2-x^2} = a\cos\theta\)
  • \(\sqrt{a^2 + x^2} \implies x = a\tan\theta,\quad dx = a\sec^2\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{a^2+x^2} = a\sec\theta\)
  • \(\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \implies x = a\sec\theta,\quad dx = a\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{x^2-a^2} = a\tan\theta\)
body.ar:
Rational الدوال (Partial Fractions): Let \(P(x)/Q(x)\) be a proper rational الدالة with \(\deg(P) < \deg(Q)\). By the Fundamental مبرهنة of الجبر, \(Q(x)\) factors over \(\mathbb{R}\) into products of linear factors \((ax+b)^m\) and irreducible quadratic factors \((ax^2+bx+c)^n\):

  • Distinct linear factor \((x-r)\): produces term \(\frac{A}{x-r}\).
  • Repeated linear factor \((x-r)^k\): produces \(\frac{A_1}{x-r} + \frac{A_2}{(x-r)^2} + \dots + \frac{A_k}{(x-r)^k}\).
  • Irreducible quadratic factor \(x^2+px+q\): produces term \(\frac{Ax+B}{x^2+px+q}\).

If \(\deg(P) \ge \deg(Q)\), كثيرة الحدود long division must be executed first to express \(P/Q = S(x) + R(x)/Q(x)\) with \(\deg(R) < \deg(Q)\).

Trigonometric Substitutions (Radical Elimination):

  • \(\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} \implies x = a\sin\theta,\quad dx = a\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{a^2-x^2} = a\cos\theta\)
  • \(\sqrt{a^2 + x^2} \implies x = a\tan\theta,\quad dx = a\sec^2\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{a^2+x^2} = a\sec\theta\)
  • \(\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \implies x = a\sec\theta,\quad dx = a\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{x^2-a^2} = a\tan\theta\)

label.en: Worked Example 6.2 — Medium: Cyclic Integration by Parts
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.2 — Medium: Cyclic Integration by Parts

body.en:
Evaluate \(I = \displaystyle \int e^{2x} \cos(3x)\,dx\).

Step 1: First application of parts.
Let \(u = \cos(3x)\) and \(dv = e^{2x}\,dx\).
Then \(du = -3\sin(3x)\,dx\) and \(v = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\).
\[ I = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) - \int \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\big(-3\sin(3x)\big)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) + \frac{3}{2}\int e^{2x}\sin(3x)\,dx \]

Step 2: Second application of parts.
For \(J = \int e^{2x}\sin(3x)\,dx\), let \(u = \sin(3x)\) and \(dv = e^{2x}\,dx\).
Then \(du = 3\cos(3x)\,dx\) and \(v = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\).
\[ J = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{3}{2}\int e^{2x}\cos(3x)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{3}{2}I \]

Step 3: Solve algebraically for \(I\).
Substitute \(J\) into \(I\):

\[ I = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) + \frac{3}{2}\left( \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{3}{2}I \right) = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) + \frac{3}{4}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{9}{4}I \]

Add \(\frac{9}{4}I\) to both sides: \(\frac{13}{4}I = \frac{e^{2x}}{4}\big(2\cos(3x) + 3\sin(3x)\big)\).
Multiplying by \(\frac{4}{13}\) and adding constant \(C\):

\[ I = \frac{e^{2x}}{13}\big(2\cos(3x) + 3\sin(3x)\big) + C \]
body.ar:
Evaluate \(I = \displaystyle \int e^{2x} \cos(3x)\,dx\).

Step 1: First application of parts.
Let \(u = \cos(3x)\) and \(dv = e^{2x}\,dx\).
Then \(du = -3\sin(3x)\,dx\) and \(v = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\).
\[ I = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) - \int \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\big(-3\sin(3x)\big)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) + \frac{3}{2}\int e^{2x}\sin(3x)\,dx \]

Step 2: Second application of parts.
For \(J = \int e^{2x}\sin(3x)\,dx\), let \(u = \sin(3x)\) and \(dv = e^{2x}\,dx\).
Then \(du = 3\cos(3x)\,dx\) and \(v = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\).
\[ J = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{3}{2}\int e^{2x}\cos(3x)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{3}{2}I \]

Step 3: Solve algebraically for \(I\).
Substitute \(J\) into \(I\):

\[ I = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) + \frac{3}{2}\left( \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{3}{2}I \right) = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos(3x) + \frac{3}{4}e^{2x}\sin(3x) - \frac{9}{4}I \]

Add \(\frac{9}{4}I\) to both sides: \(\frac{13}{4}I = \frac{e^{2x}}{4}\big(2\cos(3x) + 3\sin(3x)\big)\).
Multiplying by \(\frac{4}{13}\) and adding الثابت \(C\):

\[ I = \frac{e^{2x}}{13}\big(2\cos(3x) + 3\sin(3x)\big) + C \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium
Evaluate the indefinite integral using partial fraction decomposition:
\[ \int \frac{5x - 3}{x^2 - 2x - 3}\,dx \]
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium
احسب قيمة the indefinite integral using partial fraction decomposition:
\[ \int \frac{5x - 3}{x^2 - 2x - 3}\,dx \]

solution.en:
Factor the denominator: \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)\).
Set up partial fractions:
\[ \frac{5x - 3}{(x - 3)(x + 1)} = \frac{A}{x - 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} \implies 5x - 3 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 3) \]
Using Heaviside cover-up:
Set \(x = 3\): \(5(3) - 3 = A(3 + 1) \implies 12 = 4A \implies A = 3\).
Set \(x = -1\): \(5(-1) - 3 = B(-1 - 3) \implies -8 = -4B \implies B = 2\).
Integrate term-by-term:
\[ \int \left( \frac{3}{x - 3} + \frac{2}{x + 1} \right)dx = 3\ln|x - 3| + 2\ln|x + 1| + C = \ln\left(|x - 3|^3 (x + 1)^2\right) + C \]
solution.ar:

Set up partial fractions:
\[ \frac{5x - 3}{(x - 3)(x + 1)} = \frac{A}{x - 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} \implies 5x - 3 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 3) \]
Using Heaviside cover-up:
Set \(x = 3\): \(5(3) - 3 = A(3 + 1) \implies 12 = 4A \implies A = 3\).
Set \(x = -1\): \(5(-1) - 3 = B(-1 - 3) \implies -8 = -4B \implies B = 2\).
Integrate term-by-term:
\[ \int \left( \frac{3}{x - 3} + \frac{2}{x + 1} \right)dx = 3\ln|x - 3| + 2\ln|x + 1| + C = \ln\left(|x - 3|^3 (x + 1)^2\right) + C \]

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\frac{5x - 3}{(x - 3)(x + 1)} = \frac{A}{x - 3} + \frac{B}{x + 1} \implies 5x - 3 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 3)\) ، \(x = 3\) ، \(5(3) - 3 = A(3 + 1) \implies 12 = 4A \implies A\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

body.en:
Type I (Infinite Limits): If \(f(x)\) is continuous on \([a,\infty)\), the improper integral is defined as the limit of proper Riemann integrals:

\[ \int_a^\infty f(x)\,dx = \lim_{t \to \infty} \int_a^t f(x)\,dx \]

If the limit exists as a finite real number \(L\), the integral is said to converge to \(L\); otherwise it diverges.

The \(p\)-Integral Test on \([1, \infty)\):

\[ \int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^p}\,dx \quad \begin{cases} \text{converges to } \dfrac{1}{p-1} & \text{if } p > 1 \\ \text{diverges to } +\infty & \text{if } p \le 1 \end{cases} \]

Analytical Proof

Case 1: \(p \ne 1\). By the Power Rule:

\[ \int_1^t x^{-p}\,dx = \left[ \frac{x^{1-p}}{1-p} \right]_1^t = \frac{t^{1-p} - 1}{1-p} = \frac{1}{1-p}\left( \frac{1}{t^{p-1}} - 1 \right) \]

Evaluating the limit as \(t \to \infty\):

  • If \(p > 1\), \(p-1 > 0\), so \(\lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{1}{t^{p-1}} = 0\). The limit is \(\frac{0 - 1}{1-p} = \frac{1}{p-1}\) (converges).
  • If \(p < 1\), \(1-p > 0\), so \(\lim_{t\to\infty} t^{1-p} = \infty\) (diverges).

Case 2: \(p = 1\).

\[ \lim_{t\to\infty} \int_1^t \frac{1}{x}\,dx = \lim_{t\to\infty} [\ln x]_1^t = \lim_{t\to\infty} (\ln t - 0) = \infty \quad \text{(diverges)} \quad \blacksquare \]
body.ar:
Type I (Infinite النهايات): If \(f(x)\) is continuous on \([a,\infty)\), the improper التكامل is defined as the النهاية of proper Riemann التكاملات:

\[ \int_a^\infty f(x)\,dx = \lim_{t \to \infty} \int_a^t f(x)\,dx \]

If the النهاية exists as a finite real number \(L\), the التكامل is said to converge to \(L\); otherwise it diverges.

The \(p\)-التكامل Test on \([1, \infty)\):

\[ \int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^p}\,dx \quad \begin{cases} \text{converges to } \dfrac{1}{p-1} & \text{if } p > 1 \\ \text{diverges to } +\infty & \text{if } p \le 1 \end{cases} \]

Analytical Proof

Case 1: \(p \ne 1\). By the Power Rule:

\[ \int_1^t x^{-p}\,dx = \left[ \frac{x^{1-p}}{1-p} \right]_1^t = \frac{t^{1-p} - 1}{1-p} = \frac{1}{1-p}\left( \frac{1}{t^{p-1}} - 1 \right) \]

Evaluating the النهاية as \(t \to \infty\):

  • If \(p > 1\), \(p-1 > 0\), so \(\lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{1}{t^{p-1}} = 0\). The النهاية is \(\frac{0 - 1}{1-p} = \frac{1}{p-1}\) (converges).
  • If \(p < 1\), \(1-p > 0\), so \(\lim_{t\to\infty} t^{1-p} = \infty\) (diverges).

Case 2: \(p = 1\).

\[ \lim_{t\to\infty} \int_1^t \frac{1}{x}\,dx = \lim_{t\to\infty} [\ln x]_1^t = \lim_{t\to\infty} (\ln t - 0) = \infty \quad \text{(diverges)} \quad \blacksquare \]

label.ar: مثال محلول 6.3 — Advanced: Trigonometric Substitution with Definite Bounds

body.en:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^2 \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{16 - x^2}}\,dx\).

Step 1: Select trigonometric substitution.
The radicand has form \(a^2 - x^2\) with \(a = 4\).
Substitute \(x = 4\sin\theta\). Then \(dx = 4\cos\theta\,d\theta\) and:
\[ \sqrt{16 - x^2} = \sqrt{16(1 - \sin^2\theta)} = 4\cos\theta \quad \left(\text{for } \theta \in [0, \pi/6]\right) \]

Step 2: Transform limits of integration.
When \(x = 0\), \(4\sin\theta = 0 \implies \theta = 0\).
When \(x = 2\), \(4\sin\theta = 2 \implies \sin\theta = 1/2 \implies \theta = \pi/6\).

Step 3: Substitute and simplify.

\[ \int_0^{\pi/6} \frac{(4\sin\theta)^2}{4\cos\theta}\,(4\cos\theta\,d\theta) = 16 \int_0^{\pi/6} \sin^2\theta\,d\theta \]

Using the half-angle identity \(\sin^2\theta = \frac{1 - \cos(2\theta)}{2}\):

\[ 16 \int_0^{\pi/6} \frac{1 - \cos(2\theta)}{2}\,d\theta = 8 \left[ \theta - \frac{\sin(2\theta)}{2} \right]_0^{\pi/6} = 8\left( \frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sin(\pi/3)}{2} \right) = 8\left( \frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \right) = \frac{4\pi}{3} - 2\sqrt{3} \]
body.ar:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^2 \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{16 - x^2}}\,dx\).

Step 1: Select trigonometric substitution.
The radicand has form \(a^2 - x^2\) with \(a = 4\).
Substitute \(x = 4\sin\theta\). Then \(dx = 4\cos\theta\,d\theta\) and:
\[ \sqrt{16 - x^2} = \sqrt{16(1 - \sin^2\theta)} = 4\cos\theta \quad \left(\text{for } \theta \in [0, \pi/6]\right) \]

Step 2: Transform النهايات of integration.
When \(x = 0\), \(4\sin\theta = 0 \implies \theta = 0\).
When \(x = 2\), \(4\sin\theta = 2 \implies \sin\theta = 1/2 \implies \theta = \pi/6\).

Step 3: عوّض and بسّط.

\[ \int_0^{\pi/6} \frac{(4\sin\theta)^2}{4\cos\theta}\,(4\cos\theta\,d\theta) = 16 \int_0^{\pi/6} \sin^2\theta\,d\theta \]

Using the half-الزاوية المتطابقة \(\sin^2\theta = \frac{1 - \cos(2\theta)}{2}\):

\[ 16 \int_0^{\pi/6} \frac{1 - \cos(2\theta)}{2}\,d\theta = 8 \left[ \theta - \frac{\sin(2\theta)}{2} \right]_0^{\pi/6} = 8\left( \frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sin(\pi/3)}{2} \right) = 8\left( \frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \right) = \frac{4\pi}{3} - 2\sqrt{3} \]

body.en:
Integration by Parts Sign Error: The formula is \(\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du\). Forgetting that the second term has a MINUS sign (or mishandling double negatives when \(v\) is negative) is a chronic trap.

Choosing u via LIATE: Prioritize \(u\) in the order: Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential. Differentiating \(u\) must simplify the remaining integrand.

Partial Fractions Improper Rational Functions: The method of partial fractions ONLY applies when the numerator degree is strictly LESS than the denominator degree. If \(\deg(P) \ge \deg(Q)\), you MUST perform polynomial long division first!

Definite Integrals with U-Sub: Remember to update limits of integration: \(x = a \to u(a)\), \(x = b \to u(b)\). Evaluating using original limits on a \(u\)-expression is an automatic deduction.

Improper Discontinuous Integrands (Type II): Watch out for internal vertical asymptotes (e.g. \(\int_{-1}^1 \frac{1}{x^2}\,dx\)). You cannot blindly apply FTC: the integral diverges because \(x=0\) is an infinite discontinuity.
body.ar:
Integration by Parts Sign Error: The الصيغة is \(\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du\). Forgetting that the second term has a MINUS sign (or mishandling double negatives عندما \(v\) is negative) is a chronic trap.

Choosing u via LIATE: Prioritize \(u\) in the order: Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential. Differentiating \(u\) must بسّط the remaining integrand.

Partial Fractions Improper Rational الدوال: The method of partial fractions ONLY applies عندما the numerator degree is strictly LESS than the denominator degree. If \(\deg(P) \ge \deg(Q)\), you MUST perform كثيرة الحدود long division first!

Definite التكاملات with U-Sub: Remember to update النهايات of integration: \(x = a \to u(a)\), \(x = b \to u(b)\). Evaluating using original النهايات on a \(u\)-العبارة الجبرية is an automatic deduction.

Improper Discontinuous Integrands (Type II): Watch out for internal vertical خطوط التقارب (e.g. \(\int_{-1}^1 \frac{1}{x^2}\,dx\)). You cannot blindly apply FTC: the التكامل diverges because \(x=0\) is an infinite discontinuity.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced
Evaluate the improper integral or establish its divergence:
\[ \int_0^\infty x e^{-x/2}\,dx \]
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced
احسب قيمة the improper integral or establish its divergence:
\[ \int_0^\infty x e^{-x/2}\,dx \]

solution.en:
Express as a limit of a definite integral:
\[ \int_0^\infty x e^{-x/2}\,dx = \lim_{t \to \infty} \int_0^t x e^{-x/2}\,dx \]
Integrate by parts on \([0, t]\):
Let \(u = x \implies du = dx\), and \(dv = e^{-x/2}dx \implies v = -2e^{-x/2}\).
\[ \int_0^t x e^{-x/2}\,dx = \left[ -2x e^{-x/2} \right]_0^t - \int_0^t (-2e^{-x/2})\,dx = -2t e^{-t/2} + 0 + 2 \left[ -2e^{-x/2} \right]_0^t \]
\[ = -2t e^{-t/2} - 4\big(e^{-t/2} - 1\big) = 4 - e^{-t/2}(2t + 4) \]
Take the limit as \(t \to \infty\):
By L'Hôpital's Rule, \(\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{2t+4}{e^{t/2}} = \lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{2}{\frac{1}{2}e^{t/2}} = 0\).
Therefore:
\[ \lim_{t \to \infty} \big[4 - e^{-t/2}(2t + 4)\big] = 4 - 0 = 4 \]
solution.ar:
Express as a limit of a definite integral:
\[ \int_0^\infty x e^{-x/2}\,dx = \lim_{t \to \infty} \int_0^t x e^{-x/2}\,dx \]
Integrate by parts on \([0, t]\):
ليكن \(u = x \implies du = dx\), and \(dv = e^{-x/2}dx \implies v = -2e^{-x/2}\).
\[ \int_0^t x e^{-x/2}\,dx = \left[ -2x e^{-x/2} \right]_0^t - \int_0^t (-2e^{-x/2})\,dx = -2t e^{-t/2} + 0 + 2 \left[ -2e^{-x/2} \right]_0^t \]
\[ = -2t e^{-t/2} - 4\big(e^{-t/2} - 1\big) = 4 - e^{-t/2}(2t + 4) \]
Take the limit as \(t \to \infty\):
By L'Hôpital's Rule, \(\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{2t+4}{e^{t/2}} = \lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{2}{\frac{1}{2}e^{t/2}} = 0\).
Therefore:
\[ \lim_{t \to \infty} \big[4 - e^{-t/2}(2t + 4)\big] = 4 - 0 = 4 \]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Easy] Consider the region \(R\) in the first quadrant bounded by the curves \(y = \sqrt{x}\), \(y = 0\), and \(x = 4\). A solid is formed by revolving \(R\) about the line \(x = 5\). Determine the volume of this solid using the method of cylindrical shells. The volume can be expressed in the form \(V = k\pi \int_a^b (5 - x) \sqrt{x} \, dx\). Find the value of \(k\).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Easy] Consider the region \(R\) in the first quadrant bounded بتطبيق curves \(y = \sqrt{x}\), \(y = 0\), and \(x = 4\). A solid is formed by revolving \(R\) about the line \(x = 5\). حدّد volume of this solid باستخدام method of cylindrical shells. The volume can be expressed in the form \(V = k\pi \int_a^b (5 - x) \sqrt{x} \, dx\). أوجد قيمة \(k\).

hints.en: The region \(R\) is bounded by \(y = \sqrt{x}\), \(y = 0\), and \(x = 4\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(R\) ، \(y = \sqrt{x}\) ، \(y = 0\) ، \(x = 4\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: We are revolving this region about the vertical line \(x = 5\). We will use the method of cylindrical shells.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(x = 5\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
The region \(R\) is bounded by \(y = \sqrt{x}\), \(y = 0\), and \(x = 4\). We are revolving this region about the vertical line \(x = 5\). We will use the method of cylindrical shells. The radius of a cylindrical shell at a given \(x\) is the distance from the axis of revolution \(x=5\) to \(x\), which is \(5 - x\). The height of the shell is the difference in the y-values of the bounding curves, which is \(\sqrt{x} - 0 = \sqrt{x}\). The thickness of the shell is \(dx\). The volume of a single cylindrical shell is \(dV = 2\pi \times \text{radius} \times \text{height} \times \text{thickness} = 2\pi (5 - x) \sqrt{x} \, dx\). The region extends from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 4\). Therefore, the total volume is given by the integral:
\[V = \int_0^4 2\pi (5 - x) \sqrt{x} \, dx\] The problem states the volume can be expressed in the form \(V = k\pi \int_a^b (5 - x) \sqrt{x} \, dx\). Comparing this to our integral, we have \(a=0\), \(b=4\), and \(k=2\). Thus, the value of \(k\) is 2.

body.en:
Just as circular trigonometric functions parameterize the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\), the six hyperbolic functions parameterize the right branch of the unit hyperbola \(x^2 - y^2 = 1\) using combinations of \(e^x\) and \(e^{-x}\):

\[ \sinh x = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \cosh x = rac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad anh x = rac{\sinh x}{\cosh x} = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{e^x + e^{-x}} \]\[ \operatorname{csch} x = rac{1}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0), \qquad \operatorname{sech} x = rac{1}{\cosh x}, \qquad \coth x = rac{\cosh x}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0) \]

\(\cosh x\)Dom \(\mathbb{R}\), Rng \([1, \infty)\)\(\sinh x\)\(\operatorname{arcosh} x = \ln\! ig(x + \sqrt{x^2-1} ig)\;(x\ge 1)\), \( rac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\)
\( anh x\)Dom \(\mathbb{R}\), Rng \((-1, 1)\)\(\operatorname{sech}^2 x\)\(\operatorname{artanh} x = rac{1}{2}\ln\!\left( rac{1+x}{1-x} ight)\;(|x|<1)\), \( rac{1}{1-x^2}\)
\(\operatorname{csch} x\)Dom \(x eq 0\), Rng \(y eq 0\)\(-\operatorname{csch} x\coth x\)Odd reciprocal of \(\sinh x\)
\(\operatorname{sech} x\)Dom \(\mathbb{R}\), Rng \((0, 1]\)\(-\operatorname{sech} x anh x\)Bell-shaped reciprocal of \(\cosh x\)
\(\coth x\)Dom \(x eq 0\), Rng \(|y|>1\)\(-\operatorname{csch}^2 x\)Horizontal asymptotes \(y = \pm 1\)

Fundamental Hyperbolic Identity: \(\cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = 1\), \(1 - anh^2 x = \operatorname{sech}^2 x\), and \(\sinh(2x) = 2\sinh x\cosh x\). Physically, a flexible uniform cable hanging under gravity forms the catenary curve \(y = a\cosh(x/a)\).
body.ar:
كما تُمثّل الدوال المثلثية الدائرية دائرة الوحدة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\)، فإن الدوال الزائدية الست تُوسِّط الفرع الأيمن للقطع الزائد الواحدي \(x^2 - y^2 = 1\) بدلالة الدالتين الأسيتين \(e^x\) و\(e^{-x}\):

\[ \sinh x = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad \cosh x = rac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}, \qquad anh x = rac{\sinh x}{\cosh x} = rac{e^x - e^{-x}}{e^x + e^{-x}} \]\[ \operatorname{csch} x = rac{1}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0), \qquad \operatorname{sech} x = rac{1}{\cosh x}, \qquad \coth x = rac{\cosh x}{\sinh x}\;(x eq 0) \]
الدالةالمجال والمدىالمشتقة \( rac{d}{dx}\)الصيغة اللوغاريتمية للعكس ومشتقتها
\(\sinh x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \(\mathbb{R}\)\(\cosh x\)\(\operatorname{arsinh} x = \ln\! ig(x + \sqrt{x^2+1} ig)\)، \( rac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\)
\(\cosh x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \([1, \infty)\)\(\sinh x\)\(\operatorname{arcosh} x = \ln\! ig(x + \sqrt{x^2-1} ig)\;(x\ge 1)\)، \( rac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\)
\( anh x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \((-1, 1)\)\(\operatorname{sech}^2 x\)\(\operatorname{artanh} x = rac{1}{2}\ln\!\left( rac{1+x}{1-x} ight)\;(|x|<1)\)، \( rac{1}{1-x^2}\)
\(\operatorname{csch} x\)المجال \(x eq 0\)، المدى \(y eq 0\)\(-\operatorname{csch} x\coth x\)دالة فردية مقلوبة لـ \(\sinh x\)
\(\operatorname{sech} x\)المجال \(\mathbb{R}\)، المدى \((0, 1]\)\(-\operatorname{sech} x anh x\)منحنى جرسي متماثل مقلوب لـ \(\cosh x\)
\(\coth x\)المجال \(x eq 0\)، المدى \(|y|>1\)\(-\operatorname{csch}^2 x\)خطا تقارب أفقيان \(y = \pm 1\)

المتطابقة الزائدية الأساسية: \(\cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = 1\)، و\(1 - anh^2 x = \operatorname{sech}^2 x\)، و\(\sinh(2x) = 2\sinh x\cosh x\). فيزيائياً، يتخذ الكابل المتجانس المعلّق تحت تأثير الجاذبية شكل منحنى السلسلة \(y = a\cosh(x/a)\).
